text: $NVDA - NVIDIA DOWNGRADED TO HOLD AS $165 BILLION AI FINANCING EXPOSURE RAISES CONCERNS Aletheia Capital has downgraded Nvidia from Buy to Hold and withdrawn its $340 price target, citing growing financial risks from its AI Computing Partner program and potential internal turmoil. Analyst Stefan Chang estimates Nvidia's financial commitments have surged more than tenfold to $165 billion, including $105 billion tied to an Ohio data-center project. CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN alone could require $124 billion over the next 12–15 months, potentially rising to $450–500 billion by 2030.

text: CHINA DENIES ESPIONAGE ALLEGATIONS INVOLVING NVIDIA CEO China has rejected reports that its intelligence services targeted Nvidia ($NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang, calling the allegations groundless speculation and slander. The denial follows reports that US authorities suspect Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed International executive, of providing information to Chinese intelligence while in a relationship with Nvidia's CEO. Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into the alleged foreign intelligence operation on Sunday.

text: NETANYAHU’S OPPONENTS MOVE TO REVERSE HIS KEY POLICIES IN ISRAEL’S PARLIAMENT Newly elected opposition lawmakers in Israel, led by Gadi Eisenkot, have introduced a series of legislative proposals aimed at reversing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s key policies. Their agenda includes establishing a state commission of inquiry into the political and security failures surrounding the October 7 Hamas attacks, imposing term limits on prime ministers, and reversing the government’s judicial overhaul. The opposition also plans to repeal laws that would weaken the attorney general’s authority and increase political influence over police oversight. However, Eisenkot faces challenges in forming a governing coalition despite securing the support of 67 members of the 120-seat Knesset. The proposed bills will require parliamentary approval, while Netanyahu has criticized the opposition’s reliance on Israeli Arab parties to form a new government.

text: GOLD EDGES HIGHER AS TRADERS ASSESS US INFLATION AND FED REMARKS Gold prices edged higher by as much as 0.8% to above $4,050 an ounce in Asian trading, recovering part of the previous session’s 2.6% decline. The rebound followed stronger-than-expected US inflation data and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials, which increased expectations of another interest rate hike in December. Traders are now fully pricing in a 0.25-percentage-point Fed rate hike, creating pressure on gold as higher interest rates make the non-yielding metal less attractive. However, gold has remained above the key $4,000-an-ounce level, supported by safe-haven demand and continued central-bank purchases. Silver, platinum and palladium also recorded gains.

text: SIEMENS ENERGY SEES PROFIT SURGE BY 2030 AS POWER DEMAND BOOMS Siemens Energy AG expects its profit margins to rise to as much as 22% by 2030, driven by surging global demand for gas turbines, transformers and power-grid equipment. The German energy equipment maker forecasts annual revenue growth of up to 14% through fiscal 2030, supported by rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence infrastructure, data centers and electrification. Its profit before special items more than doubled to €5.5 billion in fiscal 2026. The company also announced an additional €9 billion share buyback through fiscal 2030 and proposed more than tripling its dividend to €2.30 per share. CEO Christian Bruch expects data-center-related electricity demand to remain strong, while the company forecasts around €5 billion in net income and €10 billion in free cash flow before tax for the current fiscal year. Its wind division, Siemens Gamesa, also reached breakeven, marking a major milestone in its turnaround.

text: WHEAT FUTURES JUMP AFTER STRIKE ON RUSSIAN BALTIC PORT Wheat futures rose sharply after a drone attack on Russia’s Ust-Luga port sparked a fire and injured three workers, raising fresh concerns over grain exports from the world’s largest wheat supplier. Ust-Luga has become an increasingly important grain-export hub as attacks in the Black Sea have disrupted shipments from Russia’s traditional agricultural ports. The port shipped 684,000 tons of grain in October, accounting for more than a quarter of Russia’s total monthly grain exports. Chicago wheat futures climbed as much as 1.6% following the attack, while the most-active contract traded 1.1% higher at $5.995 per bushel in Singapore. Markets are also monitoring Russia-Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi, where discussions are expected to include a possible Black Sea ceasefire. Meanwhile, soybeans declined 0.3%, while corn prices remained largely unchanged.

text: EUROPEAN GAS PRICES RISE AS UNCERTAINTY SWIRLS OVER IRAN WAR European natural gas prices climbed as uncertainty surrounding the Iran war and disruptions to global energy supplies heightened concerns over the region’s winter fuel availability. Benchmark Dutch gas futures rose above €85 per megawatt-hour, reaching €86.78, up 2.4%, as attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz continued and diplomatic efforts to end the conflict showed limited progress. The conflict has disrupted nearly a fifth of global liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports, intensifying competition between Europe and Asia for available supplies. Europe is facing additional pressure as LNG imports remain below last year’s levels and already-low winter gas inventories have begun declining amid the heating season. Qatar’s supply disruptions have further tightened the market, with Poland’s Orlen terminating a long-term LNG contract with QatarEnergy over delivery difficulties. Although prices have eased from recent peaks on hopes of diplomatic progress, continued supply disruptions and uncertainty over shipments through the Strait of Hormuz are keeping European gas prices elevated.

text: BANK OF AMERICA WARNS FED COULD DELIVER 50BPS HIKE IN DECEMBER Bank of America says October's hot CPI report virtually guarantees a December Fed rate hike — and opens the door to a larger 50bps move. Headline CPI rose 0.4%, while core CPI climbed 0.3%, marking a third consecutive upside inflation surprise. BofA now estimates core PCE inflation at 3.3% YoY. Price pressures are spreading across goods and services, with electronics, airfares and hotels driving increases. BofA still expects 25bps in December, but sees growing risk of another hike in January rather than March. The bank warns the Fed is falling behind inflation and calls October's decision to hold rates a potential policy mistake.

text: SAUDI OIL OUTPUT SURGES 26% AS OPEC+ RAMPS UP PRODUCTION Saudi Arabia boosted crude production by 2.19 million barrels per day in October, despite the ongoing Iran war. Output jumped from 8.37M bpd in September to 10.56M bpd, its highest level since February, according to OPEC figures cited by Reuters. Meanwhile, OPEC+ production surged 2.04M bpd to 41.23M bpd, signaling a broader recovery in supply. The sharp rebound in Middle East production could ease global oil supply pressures despite continued geopolitical tensions.

author: firstsquaw
text: Saudi Arabia Boosts Oil Production by 26% to War-Time High Saudi Arabia increased its crude oil production by 26% in October to 10.56 million barrels per day, reaching its highest level since before the war. Iraq also raised production to nearly 4.9 million barrels per day. The recovery in oil supplies, despite ongoing regional conflict and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, has contributed to falling global oil prices, with Brent crude declining approximately 21% this month to around $93 per barrel. The production surge highlights Saudi Arabia's efforts to restore oil exports and strengthen its market position amid regional tensions and competition with the UAE. Higher supplies could increase pressure on oil prices, particularly as global demand remains constrained. OPEC+ is also reviewing members' production capacities ahead of its November 29 meeting, where output targets for 2027 will be discussed.
